trajectory_summary: This is a short reschedule call, not a fresh set: a prior Ion door-knock appointment fell through, and the rep is calling to find a new time. The rep's slow, live account lookup burns the first 70+ seconds, but once oriented the call moves quickly and cleanly to a locked day, time, and hard constraint from the customer.
outcome_dispute: This call is a genuine reschedule-booking with a specific day (Monday) and time (5PM) confirmed, plus a customer-stated hard constraint (done by 05:45) the rep accepted -- this should read as 'booked', not an ambiguous or soft outcome, despite the rocky opening.

observed_outcome.quote: I'll get that set for five, and we will shoot you a reminder text just to double check that time still works for you.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday) and time (5PM) are agreed and the rep confirms he is setting it, plus commits to a reminder text -- this meets the bar for 'booked' despite the compressed button-up.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: This call is a pure reschedule of a previously-set design appointment; no utility bill, usage figure, or bill amount is discussed anywhere in the transcript.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: No mention of the utility bill document is made; the call is scoped entirely to finding a new appointment time, consistent with this being a reschedule of an already-qualified lead rather than a fresh set.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks what interested the customer in solar, and none is volunteered -- this call skips straight from account lookup to rescheduling since the qualifying conversation presumably happened at the earlier door visit.

attempt_quotes: So that's fine. No. It should be fine. Yeah. We should be able to make that work.
objections.reasoning: This is best read through protocols.time_constraint (a scheduling boundary to anchor, not an objection to overcome) -- the customer isn't resisting the appointment, she's stating a hard stop time. The rep accommodates it in one pass and the appointment proceeds, so it resolves cleanly, but the rep never restates the constraint back for confirmation or flags the shortened window against Ion's one-hour block practice.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: pre-call account prep on reschedule/callback calls
primary_coaching_focus.quote: so it looks like I pulled up the the right account here.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep spends the first 70+ seconds of a short call (00:20 through 01:13) live-searching and narrating the account history instead of opening already oriented -- this is the single biggest time-and-confidence cost on an otherwise efficient call, and it recurs three times (00:20, 00:47, 01:13), making it the clearest coachable pattern.

key_moments.stewart_read: The opening carries no company name, no reference to the prior door visit or design appointment, and no context for why the rep is calling -- the customer has to supply that ('I just got a call from you guys') before the rep re-anchors with 'this is Pike with ION' two lines later.

key_moments.quote: so it looks like I pulled up the the right account here.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is pre-call-prep failure, not knowledge_gap (knowledge_gap is about not being able to answer a customer question) -- the rep hadn't pulled up the account before dialing and is searching for it live while the customer waits.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Sorry. Just give me one more second here.
key_moments.stewart_read: A second apology for search time follows a 13-second silent gap (00:34 to 00:47) in the transcript -- compounding evidence that the rep opened the call without the account ready, costing real time on a call that otherwise runs efficiently.

key_moments.quote: Okay. It looks like, yeah, it looks like we we had time set up to share a solar design with you. It looks like a a, a week or so ago, that ended up falling through.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep is narrating CRM notes aloud to the customer in real time as he reads them, rather than opening with a pre-digested summary of what happened last time. This is the same pre-call-prep gap surfacing again at the moment it matters most -- explaining a missed appointment to the customer.
